# WorldDevKit coding-agent instructions

Canonical documentation: https://docs.kobotai.co/world
Full agent context: https://world.kobotai.co/llm.txt
Focused build instructions: https://docs.kobotai.co/world/guides/build-a-world.md
Public source: https://github.com/KobotAI/world-protocol
Protocol: world/0.1, Level 1 (read-only)
Package version: 0.2.0
Runtime: Node.js 20+

You are a coding agent. Build the world in the user's brief as a working website that also serves the World Protocol Level 1 API. Make the changes and run them; do not reply with only a plan or tutorial.

## Start

```sh
npm create worlddevkit@latest my-world
cd my-world
npm install
npm test
```

The starter already works end to end: a website at `/`, the API, sample entities and passing tests. Change three places:

- `src/data.ts`: every entity; the single source of truth for API and website.
- `src/world.ts`: name, description and public URL, via `defineWorld`.
- `public/`: the website, which reads data only through the API.

## Rules

- Level 1 is read-only. For games or anything visitors change, make it Level 2: add `actions` to `defineWorld` (sessions, capabilities gate actions, `ifVersion` prevents lost updates, `ActionError` for rule refusals, live events at `{api}/events`). Never put secrets in public entities. Test with `assertLevel2Conformance` and a two-player race.
- Scope: 2–4 entity types, 15–40 entities with relationships; one explore view designed for the domain, plus list/search and detail views.
- Work in phases: data and API with `npm run typecheck` and `npm test` passing, then the website, then tests and polish.
- Keep the list/search view as the accessible path; keep loading, empty, not-found and error states.
- Discover the API from `/.well-known/world.json`; treat cursors as opaque; only `public` entities are served.
- No database, auth, Docker or cloud services unless the brief requires them.
- `WORLD_URL` is the public origin with no path; locally it follows `PORT`.
- Report what you built, files changed, the commands you actually ran and their results, what you could not verify, and what Level 1 could not do.
